posts.title: APJ Ministries - Album Release Website
posts.excerpt: A WordPress album site built to turn listeners into supporters — player, galleries, and shop.
posts.content:
I designed and developed the album-release website for Alicia Peters-Jordan Ministries — a Richmond gospel artist whose work is built around worship, testimony, and service. The brief was not a brochure. It needed to sound like the music: inviting on first play, then deep enough to hold releases, photos, video, and a store.

I built the site in WordPress with a custom music player, image and video galleries, WooCommerce for albums such as Redeemed and In High Praise, and clear paths for booking, donations, and the ministry mission. Navigation, merchandising, and media are all tuned so a first-time visitor can listen, learn, and purchase without hunting through a generic church theme.

The result is a living catalog and campaign surface — not a one-page splash — that still looks considered on a phone in a sanctuary lobby.

seo.description: Alicia Peters-Jordan Ministries WordPress album site — music player, galleries, shop, and booking for a Richmond gospel artist.

posts.title: Frendigo App
posts.excerpt: A three-platform ride marketplace built to replace surge with subscription pricing and direct pay.
posts.content:
I am the senior lead developer on Frendigo, a three-platform transportation marketplace I architected so riders and drivers are not trapped in someone else’s surge math. Clients plan commutes, pick providers from a live marketplace, see itemized estimates before they book, and pay the provider directly. Providers set their own rates, vehicles, and add-ons — and keep more of what they earn.

I built the mobile clients in Flutter for iOS and Android, the web experience in Angular, and the realtime layer on Firebase with Google Maps for mid-trip tracking. Pricing is a subscription engine fed by MPG, USDOT, and EIA gas data rather than a per-trip commission. Reservations can be split across providers, modified after booking, and extended with backtrack when something is left behind.

The product is in TestFlight and Android beta: a full commute OS, not a skin on a rideshare clone.

posts.title: Frendigo.com
posts.excerpt: A dual-persona marketing site designed to sell the switch — commute and earnings calculators, not a brochure.
posts.content:
I designed and built Frendigo.com as the public face of a product that has to explain itself in one screen: cheap rides, great vibes — then prove it. The site splits immediately into two journeys. Clients get a marketplace story, a commute estimator, and a side-by-side of Frendigo versus opaque surge platforms. Providers get earnings logic, rate control, and a reason to leave the middleman.

I developed it in Angular with custom illustration, motion, and HTML/CSS/JS — not a theme with a form slapped on. Interactive calculators, persona routing, and campaign-ready graphics do the conversion work that a static landing page cannot. Every module is built to travel: web, app store traffic, and future ops/training properties on the same stack.

seo.title: Frendigo Marketing Website | Angular
seo.description: Frendigo.com marketing site in Angular — dual client/provider personas, commute and earnings calculators, custom graphics.

posts.title: Genworth — R70 Age Suit
posts.excerpt: An interactive Age Suit infographic built to let agents and families explore aging without the hardware.
posts.content:
I built the interactive R70 Age Suit infographic for Genworth Financial — a Fortune 500 insurer using a first-of-its-kind age-simulation suit to push long-term care into the national conversation. The physical suit (vision loss, muffled hearing, restricted joints) needed a digital twin agents and families could explore without stepping into the hardware.

I developed a custom Adobe CQ5/AEM and JavaScript experience with front, side, and back views; hover hotspots for vision, hearing, arthritis, and muscle loss; and help controls to show, hide, and explain each target. It shipped on genworth.com and inside the PRO Agent portal — the same surfaces I was managing as senior content / front-end developer.

Alongside the infographic I led the Long Term Care site onto a fully responsive layout, tagged journeys for Eloqua, and implemented Schema, Open Graph, and canonicals so the campaign could be found and shared with the gravity it deserved.
featureTags: Responsive Long Term Care site work

seo.description: Interactive R70 Age Suit infographic for Genworth — hotspots, three views, AEM/JS, on genworth.com and the PRO Agent portal.

posts.title: Industry 4.0
posts.excerpt: A plant-floor dashboard designed to put live metrics, a 3D floor plan, and escalation in one view.
posts.content:
I designed and engineered this Industry 4.0 dashboard as a serious operations surface, not a chart gallery. The problem is familiar on a plant floor: production lives in one system, alarms in another, and the floor plan on a PDF someone printed in 2017. I collapsed that into a single React application.

Operators pick a facility on Google Maps, then drop into real-time line metrics, reports, and a 3D floor plan that locates the fault instead of describing it. When a line degrades I surface the issue and the escalation path in the same view. Visualization is D3 plus custom HTML, CSS, and JavaScript — tuned for glanceability on a control-room display and still usable on a tablet on the floor.

It is a production-monitoring showcase: the kind of product UI manufacturing teams actually keep open.

seo.title: Industry 4.0 Manufacturing Dashboard | React
seo.description: Industry 4.0 manufacturing dashboard in React + D3 — facility maps, live metrics, 3D floor plan, and issue escalation.

posts.title: Lumber Liquidators Flash Sale Email Template
posts.excerpt: A flash-sale HTML email created to push hardwood deals across every major inbox.
posts.content:
I developed this flash-sale email for Lumber Liquidators — then North America’s largest specialty hardwood retailer — for campaigns that had one job: make a subscriber feel the clock. These were not newsletter layouts with a coupon code. They were event emails for time-boxed flooring promotions, built to survive Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail, and the dark art of nested tables.

I produced bulletproof HTML/CSS: hero offers, product blocks, and CTA hierarchy that held together when images were blocked and when a merchandising team swapped SKUs at the last hour. The work sat alongside a three-year run leading the responsive, ADA-minded rebuild of lumberliquidators.com — so the email visual language matched the site customers landed on.

posts.title: Muziktruck - HTML Email Development
posts.excerpt: A campaign HTML email designed to look like a brand in every major inbox, not a Mailchimp default.
posts.content:
I designed and coded Muziktruck’s campaign email from the ground up — a high-energy HTML template meant to survive the inbox and still look like a brand, not a default Mailchimp skin. Color, custom graphics, and a clear path back to the website had to work when images were off, when Gmail clipped the height, and when Outlook decided tables were a suggestion.

I built semantic, table-based HTML and inline CSS tested across major clients, with production-ready modules for future drops: new dates, new art, new links, without a redesign every send. The template is a reusable campaign system, not a one-off JPEG in a cell.

posts.title: Smallbizniz LLC
posts.excerpt: A React studio site built to sell custom work — motion, services, and packages, not a $29.99 theme.
posts.content:
I designed and developed Smallbizniz.com as the flagship for my studio: custom graphics, web and mobile apps, and 3D print/design for small businesses, churches, and nonprofits. It had to feel like the work — energetic, precise, a little defiant of the “as low as $29.99/month” internet.

I built it as a React single-page application with absolutely positioned, animated compositions, custom HTML/CSS/JS, and a service architecture that walks from craft (apps, graphics, additive manufacturing) into bundles and essentials. Motion is structural, not decorative: it paces the pitch the way a good sales conversation does.

The site is both portfolio and product — proof that a small studio site can be as considered as an enterprise flagship.

seo.title: Smallbizniz LLC — Custom React Website
seo.description: Smallbizniz.com React studio site — animated layouts, service storytelling, and a brand that sells custom work, not a theme.

It had to carry campus identity, next steps, and the tone of the house (honor, hospitality, hope) without reading like a program insert.

I took the work from concept through print: Illustrator for the mark and vector system, Photoshop for photography and finish, InDesign for the front-and-back spread, type, and press specs. posts.title: Too Smart 2 Start
posts.excerpt: A WordPress campaign system built to put the live prevention message on the homepage and the rest in a slider.
posts.content:
I designed and developed a custom WordPress content type for Henrico Too Smart 2 Start, a 501(c)3 coalition working to reduce youth substance misuse in Henrico County through education, advocacy, and capacity building. Their campaigns are the public face of that work — they needed to lead the homepage, not sit in a blog grid.

I engineered the current campaign as the hero and every other campaign into a horizontal slider, backed by a custom post type so staff can ship a new push without a developer on the call. The homepage becomes a rotating public-health billboard: one message in command, the archive still visible, the CMS boring in the best way.

posts.title: Tutor Medics
posts.excerpt: A brand system designed to make Tutor Medics unmistakable on a flyer, a card, and a counter.
posts.content:
I designed the brand style for Tutor Medics, a tutoring practice spanning K–12, college, and working professionals — virtual and in-person, subject support through test prep and social-emotional learning. The brand had to feel clinical, kind and had to survive a phone screenshot or a card left on a kitchen counter.

I created a high-contrast magenta, yellow, and blue identity in Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign: logo and brand spread, flyer, and business cards as one system, not three disconnected jobs. Type, palette, and layout lock so a parent, a principal, and a college student all read the same promise in three seconds.

posts.title: VCU Annual Report 2018-19
posts.excerpt: A digital annual report built to tell VCU’s year as chapters — student stories, overlay navigation, full-bleed type.
posts.content:
I developed Virginia Commonwealth University’s 2018–19 digital annual report on Terminal Four — a flagship storytelling piece, not a PDF with extra padding. The editorial spine was “success is”: involvement, experience, and perspective. Student stories had to feel like chapters. Leadership had to be a destination, not a masthead.

I built full-bleed color fields, oversized type, student profiles, and an overlay menu for the president’s message and key initiatives. HTML, CSS, and JavaScript sit inside T4 so university editors could still ship content without breaking the cinematic layout. It reads like a magazine and behaves like a CMS component.

seo.description: VCU 2018–19 digital annual report on Terminal Four — “success is” chapters, student stories, and overlay navigation.

posts.title: VCU Annual Report 2019-20
posts.excerpt: A digital annual report designed to tell a pandemic year as chapters — One VCU, research, and the virtual pivot.
posts.content:
I developed VCU’s 2019–20 digital annual report for a year that refused to sit still: pandemic, remote teaching, and a university that had to prove it was still one institution. President Rao’s “One VCU” frame, Medicines for All and COVID-era research, virtual commencement, athletics, and the plan to return to campus all needed a visual system that could carry gravity without looking funereal.

I built a chaptered Terminal Four experience — responsive layouts, large photography, and HTML/CSS/JS components that let the year unfold as a story instead of a stacked press release. Editors could update; the design still held the room.

posts.title: VCU Social Work Directory
posts.excerpt: A faculty directory built to search, filter, and open profiles with no third-party scripts.
posts.content:
I designed and engineered the faculty and staff directory for the VCU School of Social Work — a JSON-driven Terminal Four component that had to feel like a product, not a table dump. Researchers hunt by expertise. Students hunt by name. Staff hunt by unit. One interface, no jQuery plugin tax.

I wrote reusable vanilla JavaScript: search across name, email, and expertise; filter by unit and role; profile cards that open into credentials, expertise, and selected publications. It ships without third-party scripts so it survives university security reviews and the next CMS upgrade. Other VCU units can adopt the pattern instead of buying a directory SaaS.

posts.title: W2 OCONUS Selector
posts.excerpt: A command selector built to give Service Members abroad the right crisis and DSN contacts.
posts.content:
I developed the OCONUS selector on warfighterwellness.org because a stateside 988 banner is not enough for a Service Member in another theater. Visitors stationed outside the continental U.S. choose a combatant command — AFRICOM, CENTCOM, EUCOM, INDOPACOM, NORTHCOM, or SOUTHCOM — and the site has to answer with the right crisis-line and DSN details.

I built a homepage modal and footer flow in WordPress and custom JavaScript. The choice persists as a combatant_command query parameter so the banner, contacts, and deep links stay in sync as they move through the site. It is a small UI with outsized stakes: the right number, in the right theater, without a scavenger hunt through policy PDFs.

I built the brand header, category navigation, expanded search, and the interactive SVG map of centers in the United States, Europe, and Korea/Japan. WordPress, Advanced Custom Fields, custom SVG/JavaScript, and production HTML/CSS keep the CMS in the hands of the program while the interface still feels like a product: mission-ready, not a default theme with a stock map pin.

posts.title: Warfighter Wellness - Interactive Map
posts.excerpt: An interactive SVG map built to plot AFWC locations across the U.S., Europe, and Korea/Japan.
posts.content:
I designed and engineered the interactive SVG map that powers Armed Forces Wellness Center locations on Warfighter Wellness. Three theaters — United States, Europe, Korea/Japan — had to be readable at a glance and accurate when a center is added, moved, or renamed.

I built a custom post type and ACF metaboxes as the source of truth, then drove the map from WordPress wp-json so editors update locations without touching illustration files. Custom SVG and JavaScript handle region switching, hit areas, and detail panels. It is cartography as a CMS component: the map is the product, the admin is the ops console.

posts.title: Why VCU?
posts.excerpt: A recruitment microsite created to make VCU feel specific — campus, health system, and Richmond, not a ranking list.
posts.content:
I developed the "Why VCU?" microsite for prospective students who were already drowning in viewbooks. The job was to make Virginia Commonwealth University feel specific: two campuses, a working city, a research and health system in the same breath as student life — and to do it with interaction, not a bullet list of rankings.

I built it in Terminal Four with custom HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: interactive modules that let a visitor poke at academics, community, and Richmond without a linear scroll to nowhere. It was recruitment as product design — motion and structure in service of a decision, not a brand film with a form at the end.
